unit.sep: Construct,test matched points and justify a transformation with correspondence evidence.
unit.careers: Illustrative design,layout and geometry practices;no vehicle-operation or professional safety qualification.
unit.focus: Exact symmetry,plane-surface and scoped Cartesian reflections,inverse mirror construction and limited practical applications.
unit.phenomenon: A fictional design team claims every rectangle has diagonal symmetry and every vehicle mirror gives an equal-size complete view.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Folds,acrylic plane-mirror observation,plain-paper perpendicular bisectors,three Cartesian mirrors and an inconsistent pair set.
unit.drivingQuestion: How can we construct and test a reflection before trusting its application? KICD: How is reflection important in day-to-day activities?
unit.storylineThread: Symmetry → properties → plain construction → x=0 → y=0 → y=x → plain inverse → Cartesian consistency → application → audit → independent evidence.
unit.content: Symmetry and Reflection; Reflection on a plane surface; reflection on a Cartesian plane (mirror line to be x=0, y=0, y=x),
unit.coreCompetencies:
Learning to Learn: the learner develops relationship skills when discussing with peers the applications of reflections in real life such as use of mirrors in road transport.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner acquires connection skills when making cut outs of plane figures for finding the number of lines of symmetry.
unit.values:
Unity: the learner takes turns when working with peers to make cut outs of plane figures used reflection.
Responsibility: the learner takes care of instruments used to construct images formed after reflection in the mirror lines.
unit.pcis: Road safety: the learner discusses with peers the applications of reflections in real life such as use of mirrors in road transport.

assessment.instructions: Lesson11,40minutes:4procedure,16sections1–2,12sections3–4,4silentcheck,4collection. Work independently with RF12,blank plain paper,ruler,set square/approved compass and pencil. No teaching cards,answer cues,peer discussion or media. Keep construction lines and label all matching vertices.

sections.title: 1. Symmetry and properties
sections.prompt: Draw a non-square rectangle and an equilateral triangle;draw every symmetry line and state the number for each. Explain two properties of plane reflection,including the relationship between a point,its image and the mirror. State what happens to a point on the mirror.
sections.exemplar: Rectangle2lines through opposite-side midpoints;triangle3vertex-to-opposite-midpoint lines. Reflection preserves lengths/angles/shape/area and reverses orientation;mirror perpendicularly bisects nonfixed point-image segments. Fixed points stay on mirror. Award diagram evidence,not counts alone.

sections.title: 2. Construct images on two surfaces
sections.prompt: On blank plain paper draw a vertical mirror m;place A2cm left of it and B4cm left of it and3cm above A. Draw the reflected segment and retain perpendicular/equal-distance construction evidence. On RF12 grid draw triangle PQR and its image in the stated mirror. Give the coordinate rule and justify one pair.
sections.exemplar: Plain:Aimage2cm right at Aheight,Bimage4cm right and3cm above Aheight;segments mirror each other,construction perpendicular/equidistant. Cartesian mirror y=0:imagesP(-4,-1),Q(-1,-1),R(-3,-4);rule(x,y)→(x,-y). Check labelled drawings and right angles/equal distances.

sections.title: 3. Recover and justify a mirror
sections.prompt: For RF12 FinalB,draw the object points,image points and common mirror line;show why it fits both pairs. Explain why a single fixed point alone cannot determine a unique unrestricted mirror. State the image of(-2,3)in x=0 and in y=x to distinguish the two rules.
sections.exemplar: Mirror y=x;each joining segment has midpoint(-0.5,-0.5)on this line and is perpendicular to it. One fixed point lies on infinitely many possible unrestricted mirror lines. Images in x=0:(2,3);in y=x:(3,-2).

sections.title: 4. A useful application and its limit
sections.prompt: Explain one specific benefit of reflection in design or a plane-mirror application. State one relevant limitation. For a road-mirror example,explain why a mirror alone cannot guarantee safety and distinguish a possible curved vehicle mirror from the ideal plane mirror.
sections.exemplar: Accept justified bilateral alignment/consistent manufacture/appropriate plane-mirror observation benefit. Symmetry alone does not prove function or strength. Traffic mirrors can have restricted views/blind spots;some are convex with changed size/field,so ideal equal-size plane properties are conditional. No unsafe demonstration/driver-qualification claim. A reasoned benefit is not enduring attitude evidence.
